title: Traffic Gradient Limiter and Shadow-Apply for Safe Batching/Cache Tuning
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Add a Traffic Gradient Limiter service and a "shadow-apply" deployment mode to enable automated batching/cache configuration recommendations to be applied progressively and safely. The feature enforces latency/throughput SLO guardrails during optimistic cost-saving tuning and provides deterministic rollback triggers based on anomaly detection and SLO breaches.
background: We have several initiatives that propose more aggressive batching and cache-TTL adjustments to reduce token cost (recommendation engine work). Prior attempts to apply wide-scope changes caused tail-latency regressions on a small set of customers and required emergency rollbacks. This ticket implements a conservative, automated control plane that can: 1) apply config changes gradually using a traffic gradient, 2) observe shadowed config effects before live cutover, and 3) trigger automated rollback or fallback routing when SLOs degrade.
solution_overview: Introduce a Traffic Gradient Limiter (TGL) microservice that orchestrates traffic percentage ramps per route/customer, enforces per-route limiters (max batch size, effective concurrency), and feeds observed metrics into an Anomaly Scoring Engine. Add a 'shadow-apply' execution path in the runner so that new batching/cache config is executed in parallel for a sampled subset of requests (no downstream commit) and compared against the golden path. The system performs a canary ramp (0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) with safety gates: quantitative SLO checks (p99 latency, throughput, error rate) and qualitative checks (model output divergence threshold). If gates fail, rollback to the prior configuration and route traffic to a compatible fallback variant.
design_decisions: Fail-open vs fail-closed: default to fail-open for user requests (avoid 5xx) but rollback tuning changes if SLOs degrade repeatedly.
Centralized TGL vs per-region agents: start centralized control plane for faster iteration; plan per-region agents in next phase for network-local ramping.
Shadow sampling rate: 1% of requests for initial verification, configurable per-customer for high-risk orgs.
Anomaly scoring: combine EWMA on tail latency, z-score on 1m/5m windows, and nonparametric drift detection for distribution shifts.
Routing fallback: prefer compatible model variant fallback rather than full traffic diversion when cache/batch tuning causes instability.
Operator controls: expose manual abort and throttle-to-zero buttons in Console alongside automated policies.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: unit + integration tests in CI, feature flag behind runtime-1.22 and 'tgl-shadow-apply'.
Phase 1 (internal canary): enable on staging for 48h with synthetic load and K6 scenarios. Observe shadow diffs and p99 latency < SLO*1.05.
Phase 2 (customer canary): pick 3 low-impact customers (consent required) for live canary at 1% traffic for 24h, then 5% for 12h, evaluate metrics.
Phase 3 (ramp): automated ramp rules: 0 -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with minimum observation windows (5m at <5%, 15m at >5%).
Phase 4: full rollout with monitoring dashboards and postmortem playbook ready.
rollback_triggers: p99 latency increase > 20% over baseline for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows
error rate increase (4xx/5xx) > 1% absolute or 3x relative baseline
throughput drop > 15% correlated with batch/cache change
anomaly score > 0.95 for 5m (combines z-score and drift detectors)
model output BLEU/ROUGE-style divergence above configured threshold for structured outputs
monitoring_and_alerting: New Grafana dashboard 'TGL: per-route SLO & shadow-diff' (link in links).
Alert: TGL-SLO-Breach on p99 > threshold for >3 windows -> auto-pause ramp and page oncall.
Alert: Shadow-Diff-High when shadow path outputs diverge beyond configured tolerance -> create ticket and pause for manual review.
KPI tracking: cost-per-token delta, average batch size, cache hit ratio, and per-route latency tail.
tests: Unit: limiter logic, ramp scheduler, and anomaly score functions.
Integration: run runner with shadow-apply enabled; verify no downstream side-effects and metric tagging.
Load: K6 scenarios replicating 3 production traffic shapes (spiky, steady-high, long-tail).
Chaos: inject slow GPU kernels and network latency to validate rollback triggers behave as expected.
Regression: ensure existing autoscaling and fallback policies are not disrupted.

updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after incident review (INC-2026-02-27) where an aggressive caching change impacted p99 for a subset of customers.
2026-03-03: Spike prototyping anomaly scoring using EWMA + z-score; found 12% of historical incidents would have been detected within first 5 minutes.
2026-03-06: TGL API v0 implemented; basic ramp scheduler validated in staging with synthetic load.
2026-03-08: Shadow-apply runner integrated; initial k6 runs show <0.5% overhead for sampled requests.
2026-03-10: Start internal canary in staging. Key next step: finalize alert thresholds and update Console UI spec.
acceptance_criteria: TGL can ramp traffic per-route according to configured schedule and respect manual aborts.
Shadow-apply observes and records per-request diffs without changing customer-visible state.
Automated rollback triggers fire under synthetic regressions in load tests and successfully revert configs.
Alerts created and tested end-to-end with oncall paging (SRE runbook updated).
Documentation and Console controls are available for internal operators.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Shadow path performance overhead causes additional load. Mitigation: Keep sample rates low (1%) and limit expensive ops in shadow path.
Risk: False positives from anomaly detector. Mitigation: Combine multiple signals and require sustained breach before auto-rollback.
Risk: Ramp scheduler bug causing sudden wide-release. Mitigation: safe defaults, circuit-breaker on controller, integration tests + feature-flag gating.
